title: Trie Journey
description: Prefix comparison, trie design, terminal markers, deletion, wildcard queries, and word-search pruning.

prerequisites: Backtracking before the final board-search milestone
journey.outcome: Represent shared prefixes once, distinguish prefixes from complete words, and use the index to prune larger searches.

connections.longest-common-prefix: Start with the idea of shared prefixes before building a new data structure. Compare characters until the first disagreement or the end of the shortest word.
connections.implement-trie-prefix-tree: Store shared prefixes as tree paths. A terminal marker distinguishes a complete inserted word from a path that exists only because a longer word shares its prefix.
connections.count-words-in-trie: Traverse the structure you just built and count terminal markers, not leaves. A word can end at an internal node when it is also another word's prefix.
connections.delete-word-from-trie: Remove one word without removing shared prefixes needed by other words. Clearing the terminal marker and pruning unused nodes are separate responsibilities.
connections.replace-words: Use early terminal detection as a query operation. The first root-word endpoint encountered while traversing a sentence word is its shortest valid replacement.
connections.design-add-and-search-words-data-structu: Extend exact trie traversal with wildcard branching. A literal follows one edge, while a wildcard must consider every existing child at that depth.
connections.word-search: Learn the board-search state separately before combining it with the trie. A path consumes adjacent cells, and a cell is unavailable only for the current recursive path.
connections.word-search-ii: Combine board backtracking with prefix pruning. Advance a trie node alongside the board path, stop missing prefixes immediately, and deduplicate words found through multiple paths.
